title: Le Chatelier's principle

draft.title: Le Chatelier's principle
card: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts in the direction that partly undoes the change. It does not fully undo it.
adding a substance shifts the system to use it up. Removing a substance shifts the system to make more of it.
for a gas system in a container, raising the pressure by reducing the volume shifts the system to the side with fewer moles of gas. Lowering the pressure shifts it to the side with more moles of gas.
raising the temperature shifts the system in the endothermic direction, which absorbs heat. Lowering the temperature shifts it in the exothermic direction, which releases heat.
draft.remember: The system shifts to partly oppose whatever change was made to it.

a.q: N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) is at equilibrium in a closed container. More H2 is added at constant temperature. What happens?
opts: The system shifts right and uses up some of the added H2
The system shifts left and makes more N2
The system shifts right and all of the added H2 is used up
The system does not shift, because only pressure matters
a.why: Adding H2 is a rise in the concentration of a reactant. The system shifts right to use some of it up. It only partly undoes the change, so not all of the added H2 is used up.
a.clue: The system works to use up what was added.

b.q: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) is at equilibrium in a sealed cylinder. The volume is reduced at constant temperature, so the pressure rises. What happens?
opts: It shifts right, to the side with fewer moles of gas
It shifts left, to the side with more moles of gas
It shifts right, because the reaction is exothermic
It does not shift, because the temperature is unchanged
b.why: The left side has 3 moles of gas and the right side has 2. Higher pressure shifts the system to the side with fewer moles of gas, which is to the right. Unchanged temperature does not stop a shift caused by pressure.
b.clue: Count the moles of gas on each side.

a.best: The system shifts right and uses up some of the added H2

b.best: It shifts right, to the side with fewer moles of gas
